question: E058 was a surprise. Its prior was 0.10, yet freezing block 1 for the last 20% of samples (FreezeOut-style) cut time by 4.8%, bringing the tip from 4.93 s to 4.70 s, and accuracy was 0.7537. That is only 0.07 pp above the 0.753 gate, and the accuracy delta of about -0.08 pp is within re-draw noise. This opens an axis the tree never mapped: progressive layer freezing as a compute schedule. What does the literature say about how to schedule layer freezing in short-horizon CNN training? Specifically: (a) how early, and in what order, early layers or blocks can be frozen before accuracy drops, and whether freeze timing should follow the lr schedule or a per-layer convergence signal (gradient norm, weight change, representation similarity / SVCCA); (b) whether a second block (block 2) or partial freezing (the BN affine params or the first conv only) can be frozen too; (c) how freezing interacts with weight averaging (lookahead/EMA), BatchNorm running statistics, and normalized or orthogonalized optimizers such as Muon; (d) whether the freed compute is better spent on extra late-phase steps, to win back the accuracy margin at equal time.

rubric: Freezes (stops gradient computation and updates of) a subset of layers or blocks partway through training, with the explicit aim of reducing training compute or wall-clock time, and reports the accuracy versus time/FLOP tradeoff

Gives a concrete freezing schedule or criterion (which layers, when, in what order — e.g. lr-tied, gradient-norm, weight-change or representation-similarity based) that can be applied to a ~3-block CNN trained for a few epochs
Evaluates on image classification CNNs (ResNet/VGG/airbench-like, CIFAR or ImageNet) and reports accuracy at matched or reduced training time, ideally on short or budgeted runs
Bonus: addresses interaction with BatchNorm statistics, weight averaging (EMA/lookahead/SWA), or normalized/orthogonalized optimizers (Muon, LARS)
exclude: Methods relying on pretrained weights, transfer learning or fine-tuning of pretrained backbones (forbidden: training must be from scratch)
Methods using external data, distillation from an externally pretrained teacher, or test-set information / test-time augmentation
Freezing for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of LLMs or transformers only, with no from-scratch training result
Federated or distributed-communication freezing schemes where the gain is network bandwidth, not GPU compute
Pruning or sparsity methods that change the inference model rather than skip training compute
